sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 WebGPURenderer (WebGPU, WebGL 2 fallback); Rapier 0.19.3; Web Audio; Gamepad API; AI Hub Session Protocol v1/client 1.4.0; WebRTC
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded geometry, ink outlines, midnight teal, acid yellow and coral
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and keyframe clips for wingbeats and engine flames; procedural formations and effects
sourceInformation.audio: Code-only synthesized surf/synth score at 10% default, combat effects, formant-based gibberish voices
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world co-op for 1–4 players; direct WebRTC co-op for two; local two-player co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium WebGPU and WebGL 2 visual fallback; three scripted complete campaigns plus default attract campaign; emulated standard gamepad; phone touch; OfflineAudioContext; real two-page WebRTC; AI Hub 2/4-player, latency 150 ms, jitter 50 ms, loss 5%, host-leave and dedicated-server harness. Physical controller, listening and strict-NAT reachability unknown.
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge. Linked AI Hub integration source was read as required.

testingFeedback: 14 issues caught through automated tests, visual checks and integration review, all corrected: menu repeat, autoplay aim, remote gamepad routing, remote mouse/touch routing, guest results, host replay, remote animation, paused remote input, title wrapping, touch prompts, saved settings labels, controller credits scrolling, result preservation after peer disconnect, and stationary mouse focus interference.
3 classified as critical for the online experience: remote controller routing, missing guest results, and a victory overwritten by peer disconnect. No known remaining critical failures.
Repeated complete campaign playthroughs caught an intermittent autoplay aiming stall; the multiplayer harness verified authority, departures and network impairment.
The software WebGPU screenshot was blank; state assertions and WebGL 2 fallback screenshots provided useful verification instead.
engineFeedback: Three.js geometry, node materials and native AnimationMixer made procedural ink silhouettes and expressive wingbeats straightforward.
Initial autoplay aimed behind moving targets; predictive aim and regular pulses resolved it. Software WebGPU screenshots were blank in this headless environment.
The fixed-step arcade simulation, combat behaviors, controller-first menu/input system, synth score and authoritative network snapshots.
Coordinating asynchronous WebGPU rendering with fixed-step Rapier sensor contacts and replicated world state.
A built-in toon and outline pipeline with identical behavior across WebGPU and WebGL.
promptFeedback: The concrete controller-first philosophy, source-inspired mechanics, attract mode and explicit verification requirements.
Standalone multiplayer topology and expected campaign duration were unspecified; chose manual WebRTC plus AI Hub sessions.
Completing and verifying a cohesive six-encounter campaign, all input methods and shared-world multiplayer in a single HTML file.
Specify whether relay-backed internet connectivity is required and give a target campaign duration.

aiHub.name: Demon Rumble
aiHub.tagline: They split. You shoot. Hell of a night.
aiHub.description: An ink-soaked arcade sky battle inspired by Demon Attack. Blast splitting demons across six nights, catch forkfire power-ups, and face the Big Bad Rumble solo or with wingmates.
aiHub.controls: Stick / A,D move; Cross / Space / click fire; Circle / Shift dash; Square / E / right click pulse; Options / Esc pause; touch drag with auto-fire.
